newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan rebels say capture Kunar province.
newsitem.headline: Afghan rebels say capture Kunar province.

text.p: The rebel Taleban Islamic militia said on Friday it had captured pro-government Kunar province in eastern Afghanistan without fighting after an overnight advance from adjoining Nangarhar province.
A Taleban source, who did not want to be named, said the militia had taken control of the provincial capital of Asadabad.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.

Asked why there was no fighting, the Taleban source at the militia's office in the northwestern Pakistani town of Peshawar told Reuters by telephone that local people were already awaiting the arrival of Taleban forces to take control.

Earlier on Friday a Pakistan-based, Afghan news service quoted Taleban sources as saying the militia had taken Mehtar Lam, capital of the adjoining, pro-government Lagham province, and were advancing to the mountainous Alising and Alingar valley north of it.
The Afghan Islamic Press quoted the sources as saying the militia met little resistance when they entered Mehtar Lam town before dawn on Friday because its defenders had already fled.
